stories.title: Transfer target Julian Alvarez booed by fans in Atletico Madrid win
stories.summary: Argentinian striker was targeted by fans while warming up and jeered again after coming on in the 66th minute. Giuliano Simeone delivered a family rescue act in the dying moments, earning Atletico Madrid a dramatic 2-2 draw with Villarreal after his father Diego’s side had been reduced to 10 men on a scorching afternoon of fan anger towards European transfer target Julian Alvarez. The hosts appeared ready to collapse after Robin Le Normand was sent off in the 76th minute for bringing down Georges Mikautadze, who converted the resulting penalty to put Villarreal ahead in the Spanish league on Sunday. But Atletico found one last burst on the counterattack as Alex Baena released Giuliano down the right and the manager’s son kept his cool, sliding a delicate finish beyond goalkeeper Luiz Junior. The match had been simmering with tension long before the late drama, with Atletico supporters turning their frustration on Alvarez. The striker was booed while warming up, jeered again when his name was announced among the substitutes, and met with louder whistles when he came on in the 66th minute. A section of the crowd chanted: “Let him leave once and for all, let him leave” after Alvarez had revealed at the World Cup that he had spoken to the club about a possible transfer to “fulfil my dream”, with Barcelona heavily linked in Spanish media reports. The hostility followed him beyond the final whistle as he headed straight to the changing room while teammates saluted the fans, drawing another heavy round of boos. Atletico manager Diego Simeone confirmed that Alvarez had been advised by the club to leave the pitch after the match. “The club decided he should not go near the stands or the fans,” the Argentinian said in a news conference. “It was the club’s decision to keep him away and separate him, so he could go to the locker room.” Asked what advice he would give the under-fire Alvarez, Simeone responded: “I’m not here to give advice.”

Giuliano Simeone delivered a family rescue act in the dying moments, earning Atletico Madrid a dramatic 2-2 draw with Villarreal after his father Diego’s side had been reduced to 10 men on a scorching afternoon of fan anger towards European transfer target Julian Alvarez.

The hosts appeared ready to collapse after Robin Le Normand was sent off in the 76th minute for bringing down Georges Mikautadze, who converted the resulting penalty to put Villarreal ahead in the Spanish league on Sunday.
But Atletico found one last burst on the counterattack as Alex Baena released Giuliano down the right and the manager’s son kept his cool, sliding a delicate finish beyond goalkeeper Luiz Junior.
The match had been simmering with tension long before the late drama, with Atletico supporters turning their frustration on Alvarez.
The striker was booed while warming up, jeered again when his name was announced among the substitutes, and met with louder whistles when he came on in the 66th minute.

A section of the crowd chanted: “Let him leave once and for all, let him leave” after Alvarez had revealed at the World Cup that he had spoken to the club about a possible transfer to “fulfil my dream”, with Barcelona heavily linked in Spanish media reports.
The hostility followed him beyond the final whistle as he headed straight to the changing room while teammates saluted the fans, drawing another heavy round of boos.
Atletico manager Diego Simeone confirmed that Alvarez had been advised by the club to leave the pitch after the match.
“The club decided he should not go near the stands or the fans,” the Argentinian said in a news conference.
“It was the club’s decision to keep him away and separate him, so he could go to the locker room.”
Asked what advice he would give the under-fire Alvarez, Simeone responded: “I’m not here to give advice.”

stories.title: Parandur airport in Chennai scrapped by CM Vijay: What was the project?
stories.summary: CM Vijay has said that a new terminal, Terminal 5, would be developed in the north-western area of Chennai airport. Local villagers and farmers in Parandur had been protesting against the airport since 2022.

stories.title: Indonesia will build trustworthy commodity exchange, chief supervisor candidate Sarjito says
stories.summary: The commodity bourse is set to start operations on Jan 1.
article_sentences: Indonesia plans to start a minerals and strategic commodity exchange on Jan 1 to better control commodity prices.
Sarjito, the President’s nominee to regulate commodity trading, emphasised the need for a transparent and trustworthy market to gain trader confidence.
The regulator OJK and stakeholders must work together immediately to ensure the exchange is trusted from its first transaction, Sarjito said.
Indonesia’s upcoming minerals and strategic commodity exchange would be built with infrastructure that can be trusted, the President’s nominee to regulate commodity trading said on Aug 24.
The commodity bourse is set to start operations on Jan 1, in a move by the government of the resource-rich country to better influence prices of its commodities.
Indonesia is the world’s biggest exporter of thermal coal, palm oil and nickel.
It is also a major supplier of tin, copper, bauxite, and coffee beans.

“People will always assess the market, whether it is transparent, fair, orderly, liquid, or not,” Sarjito said at a “fit-and-proper” hearing conducted by Parliament’s financial committee for the role, which will supervise and regulate trading at the new bourse.
“If the market is not deep, has no integrity, industry players and traders would not trust it,” said Sarjito, who goes by one name.
He is President Prabowo Subianto’s sole candidate for the position of chief supervisor of commodity trading at the financial services authority, which is known locally as OJK.
Sarjito, who retired in 2024 as the OJK’s deputy commissioner of consumer protection, the highest position for a bureaucrat at the authority, needs parliamentary approval to secure the new role.
He told lawmakers that the OJK as the regulator, the bourse, clearing agencies, warehouses and other stakeholders must immediately work to build market trust.
